ai.description: This 30–40 mm frog is brown with dark mottling. It features a pointed snout, granular skin, and distinct, expanded toe discs. It inhabits stream-side vegetation in the Western Ghats.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Coorg Night Frog is best distinguished by the distinct, pale-colored, fleshy tips on its fingers and toes, which are significantly more prominent than in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Coorg Night Frog inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at altitudes between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Coorg Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in leaf litter or near streams during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus sanctipalustris* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–40 eggs on rocks or vegetation near streams, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Coorg Night Frog is endemic to the central Western Ghats, primarily inhabiting the Kodagu and Hassan districts of Karnataka at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Coorg Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" chirps, typically heard from vegetation near fast-flowing streams in Western Ghats rainforests.
